identity.name: POWER MECH PROJECTS LTD.
identity.industry: Power-plant EPC, erection & long-term O&M services + Mine Developer-cum-Operator (MDO)

summary.oneLiner: Power Mech is transitioning from a pure power-erection contractor to an integrated BOP-EPC + recurring O&M + MDO mining player, riding a multi-year thermal-power capex super-cycle (visibility to FY30) with margin uplift coming from rising O&M/MDO mix.

one-line thesis: Power Mech is transitioning from a pure power-erection contractor to an integrated BOP-EPC + recurring O&M + MDO mining player, riding a multi-year thermal-power capex super-cycle (visibility to FY30) with margin uplift coming from rising O&M/MDO mix.
financial scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | FY26 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 2,121 cr | +13% | INR 6,107 cr (~6,062 cited) | +16% |
| EBITDA | INR 237 cr (11.17% margin) | +2% | INR 750 cr (12.3% margin) | +16% |
| PAT | INR 153 cr (7.27% margin) | +18% | INR 412 cr | +18% |
| Order backlog (incl MDO) | INR 55,151 cr | — | executable ex-MDO INR 15,899 cr (+10.5% from 14,387) | — |
| Order inflow FY26 | — | — | INR 7,210 cr (vs 10,000 target; 72% achieved) | — |

One-offs / quality flags: Q4 EBITDA margin compression driven by higher operating cost + lower other income. INR 4.5 cr provision created for gratuity (Labor Code: basic rises 40%→50%). Operating cash flow surged from INR 74 lakh (FY25) to INR 430 cr (FY26) on receivables realization. Gross debt INR 622 cr / net debt INR 163 cr; D/E 0.32x. FY26 order inflow missed target mainly due to cancellation of a INR 1,563 cr BESS order by West Bengal SEB (to be re-tendered).
guidance (verify next quarter):
- **FY27 revenue: ~21% growth** (CFO explicitly confirmed it is revenue, not order growth). FY26 had targeted ~6,500 cr, achieved ~6,062; "actual shortfall only INR 438 cr" after offsetting water-division delays.
- **FY27 order inflow target: INR 12,000 cr** (FY28 range INR 12,000–15,000 cr). Opportunity basket tracked: ~INR 70,000 cr; bids ~INR 40,000–50,000 cr; historical hit ratio ~15%.
- **FY27 EBITDA: ~12.5% (incl other income), +0.25–0.3%** vs 12.3%. Long-term: +~0.5%/yr to ~14% by FY30, ~14.25% FY31.
- **MDO FY27: INR 500 cr** (KBP INR 350 cr + SAIL/Tasra INR 150 cr); FY28 INR 1,250 cr (KBP 500 + Tasra 750). MDO mix 7% of revenue FY27 → 13% FY28.
order book & pipeline:
- Total backlog INR 55,151 cr incl MDO; ex-MDO executable INR 15,899 cr. Power ~70% / non-power ~30% of backlog. Average order tenure 2.5 yrs; ~40% of opening OB executed each year.
- Power opportunity: ordering on BHEL/L&T packages ~INR 2.8 lakh cr → addressable for Power Mech ~INR 60,000 cr (installation, civil, structural, BOP).
- Client concentration: Adani 6,400 MW / ~INR 3,166–3,200 cr ongoing; BHEL 7,000 MW thermal + 1,400 MW nuclear; with Singareni BOP (INR 2,550 cr) total BHEL packages ~INR 4,700 cr.
- New verticals booked FY26: Singareni 800MW BOP EPC (from BHEL); Mumbai Monorail/Light Metro O&M (INR 279 cr); 16MW solar plant Bihar. L1 positions: Bangalore Metro, Monorail (April).
- FY27 pipeline: 2–3 BOP bids worth ~INR 15,000 cr (target win 1); BALCO O&M ~INR 1,500 cr; Butibori 2x300MW O&M ~INR 700 cr; NMDC EPC/mine-handling ~INR 8,000–10,000 cr (with thyssenkrupp); steel plants (ArcelorMittal Vizag, JSW Paradip/Gadchiroli, Bokaro, Rourkela); coal gasification (govt INR 37,500 cr plan, early stage).
segment / subsidiary:
- **Power (57% Q4 / 64% FY26 of revenue)** — installation/erection, civil, structural, O&M, now BOP EPC.
- **Non-power (43% Q4 / 36% FY26)** — civil infra, railways, water, metro O&M, MDO.
- **MDO**: KBP mine (started Nov, 1.6mt FY26, INR 248 cr rev over 5 months; March alone INR 117 cr exceptional); SAIL/Tasra (INR 106 cr FY26, washery completing Dec-26, production from mid-Q4 FY27). EBITDA ~15% now → ~20% at peak rate capacity (KBP FY30, SAIL/Tasra FY29). Full-capacity revenue ~INR 2,100–2,200 cr (4mt SAIL + 5mt KBP). NOTE: FY28 MDO guide CUT from prior INR 1,800–1,900 cr to INR 1,250 cr (conservative ramp + CCL washery not ready).
- **Water division**: drag on margins. Order INR 2,700 cr, INR 1,800 cr executed, INR 900 cr balance (INR 700 cr to execute, INR 200 cr WIP). INR 90 cr receivable + INR 128 cr uncertified pending. Execution paused; shifting ~500 schemes to O&M (300+ done) for fixed monthly state revenue. Not taking new water work.
growth verticals / optionality:
- BOP EPC scale-up (40% value-add in-house, 60% E&P outsourced) — re-rating optionality if win rate holds.
- Metro/light-rail O&M outsourcing (1,095 km operational → 2,000 km) — recurring, new TAM.
- Nuclear civil (2x700MW Kaiga INR 563 cr; India target 8,800MW→1 lakh MW; SMRs 200–250MW; US supply-chain talks) — long-dated optionality.
- Mine-site mechanization / NMDC BOT & EPC (with thyssenkrupp); steel-plant construction (INR 10 lakh cr sector capex over 5–6 yrs).
- Coal gasification (govt INR 37,500 cr) — early-stage tracking.
- International: ~INR 300–350 cr Middle East O&M (1,500 headcount), Nigeria captive O&M (~INR 100 cr), West Africa expansion (Senegal, Liberia).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Blended FY26 EBITDA 12.3% (incl other income). O&M 15–16%; construction/erection/civil <8–10%; MDO 15–16% now → 20% peak.
- Domestic input inflation (steel, cement, diesel) largely passed through via PVC/escalation clauses; international is pure O&M manpower so insulated. West-Asia war: minimal impact (intl only 1.2–1.5% of OB, ~4–5% revenue export mix).
- Margin uplift thesis = rising O&M + MDO + EPC mix.
capex / expansion: - FY27 capex INR 400 cr at Power Mech level (no debt); plus INR 400 cr in Tasra SPV (coal handling plant + railway siding) and washery construction.
capital allocation: - Low leverage (D/E 0.32x); strong OCF turnaround (INR 430 cr). MDO/Tasra capex funded without incremental debt at parent. Focus on shifting mix toward higher-margin recurring O&M to lift profitability and reduce working-capital borrowing.
risks & watch-items:
- Order-inflow guidance reliability (missed FY26 by ~28%; BESS cancellation). Verify FY27 INR 12,000 cr inflow tracking.
- MDO ramp risk — guidance already cut; CCL washery dependency, monsoon seasonality, single-month (March) revenue spike not sustainable run-rate.
- Water division receivable/certification overhang (central-govt fund release dependent).
- Labor availability (40,000+ headcount, 70–75% labor; civil labor from WB/Odisha/Jharkhand/UP) and attrition.
- BHEL packaging-philosophy change could pressure pricing/qualification on installation orders.
- Commodity inflation on fixed-price portions not covered by PVC.
management quality / tone: Confident, bullish, granular on numbers — CFO gave specific mine economics, margin bridges, and candidly acknowledged the order-inflow miss and the MDO guidance cut (conservative framing). Transparent on water-division drag. Tone credible; repeatedly emphasized power-sector visibility to FY30 and O&M-led margin improvement.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The MDO FY28 guidance was quietly cut ~35% (INR ~1,850 cr → INR 1,250 cr) vs the Feb-26 call — a key negative not flagged in the opening remarks.
- March-26 MDO revenue (INR 117 cr) was an exceptional client-driven offtake spike; normalized run-rate is INR 40–50 cr/month — investors extrapolating Q4 MDO (INR 226 cr) would overstate FY27.
- "EPC" segment now replaces the discontinued Transmission/Electricals division; railway work folded into civil — segment-label change, not pure new growth.
- The thermal thesis is explicitly a renewable-integration play: management argues 150→300GW solar creates grid imbalance requiring more thermal for night/day-night operation — a contrarian-sounding but coherent grid-stability argument.
- Receivables-driven OCF jump (74 lakh → 430 cr) is the single biggest balance-sheet positive and underappreciated vs the headline order-miss narrative.

| Solar growth (150→300GW) creating grid imbalance → more thermal night/day-night ops | POWERMECH · 539302; BHEL (code unverified) | Pure-RE EPC players reliant on stable grid | Reinforces thermal capex; Power Mech rides erection+O&M demand. Med |
| Rising O&M outsourcing (power, captive, metro 1,095→2,000 km) | POWERMECH · 539302 | In-house/incumbent O&M setups of metro cos | Recurring high-margin (15–16%) annuity; Metro O&M (INR 279 cr) a new beachhead. High |
| MDO ramp delays (CCL washery, monsoon, conservative offtake) | — | POWERMECH · 539302 | FY28 MDO guide cut ~35%; revenue visibility softer than prior call. Med |
| Water-division certification/fund delays | — | POWERMECH · 539302 | Margin & receivable drag; INR 900 cr stuck pending central-govt funds. Med |
| Domestic input inflation (steel/cement/diesel) | POWERMECH · 539302 (PVC-protected) | Fixed-price EPC peers without escalation cover | PVC/escalation clauses pass costs through; uncovered peers squeezed. Med |
| Steel-sector capex (~INR 10 lakh cr): ArcelorMittal, JSW, SAIL plants | POWERMECH · 539302 | — | Leverages Dolvi/Ballari/JSPL Angul references for civil+erection. Med-Low (IISCO bid lost on price) |
| NMDC iron-ore expansion (60→110 mt, INR 70,000 cr) | POWERMECH · 539302 (with thyssenkrupp, code unverified) | — | Qualified for mine-handling EPC/BOT; ~INR 8,000–10,000 cr pipeline. Med |

- FY26 order inflow INR 7,210 cr vs INR 10,000 cr target (72%) — primary miss = INR 1,563 cr WB BESS cancellation (to be re-tendered FY27).
- New L1 wins surfaced: Bangalore Metro, Monorail (April).
- FY27 order inflow target raised to INR 12,000 cr (FY26 target was 10,000).
- OCF jumped from INR 74 lakh (FY25) to INR 430 cr (FY26).
- New gratuity provision INR 4.5 cr (Labor Code basic 40%→50%).

themes.title: Power generation & utilities - baseload + new capacity
themes.need: Record peak demand and a thermal+hydro+nuclear capacity-addition cycle underpin regulated and merchant generators plus their service chain. NTPC/JSWENERGY/TATAPOWER/TORNTPOWER/ADANIPOWER add thermal + RE; NHPC/SJVN/NLCINDIA on hydro/lignite; TRITURBINE/TDPOWERSYS/GVPIL on turbines/generators & aftermarket; POWERMECH on EPC + O&M.
themes.driver: Peak-demand/PLF strength; new-unit commissioning; FGD + thermal-aftermarket order conversion.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "India's Market leader in O&M services having a presence across 75 GW+ unit capacity across industrial, infrastructure assets & power segments" and "India's largest O&M service provider with ~16% market share in Power O&M".
- "Strong positioning in EPC and O&M, offering an E2E capability from erection to operations" built on "5 complementary segments - Erection, Testing & Commissioning, O&M, Civil Construction, EPC and MDO".
- "Diversified Engineering and Infrastructure execution based on strong technical services" - "From power-plant construction to metro, water, and civil infra with 27 years of multi-sector project delivery with engineering depth and reliability".
- "Proven expertise in executing complex, large-scale and technology-intensive projects across geographies, driving consistent delivery excellence - a key competitive edge", supported by "11k+ trained technical workforce deployed across global projects".
- "Sustainable & overseas growth over the years" - "Strong, growing overseas presence and disciplined financial performance driving high profitability"; the track record cites 9,262 MW commissioned in overseas markets and 11.8 lakh inch metres of piping at Dangote, Nigeria.

- **FY27 EBITDA: ~12.5% (incl other income), +0.25–0.3%** vs 12.3%. Long-term: +~0.5%/yr to ~14% by FY30, ~14.25% FY31.
- **MDO FY27: INR 500 cr** (KBP INR 350 cr + SAIL/Tasra INR 150 cr); FY28 INR 1,250 cr (KBP 500 + Tasra 750). MDO mix 7% of revenue FY27 → 13% FY28.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- BOP EPC scale-up (40% value-add in-house, 60% E&P outsourced) — re-rating optionality if win rate holds.
- Metro/light-rail O&M outsourcing (1,095 km operational → 2,000 km) — recurring, new TAM.
- Nuclear civil (2x700MW Kaiga INR 563 cr; India target 8,800MW→1 lakh MW; SMRs 200–250MW; US supply-chain talks) — long-dated optionality.
- Mine-site mechanization / NMDC BOT & EPC (with thyssenkrupp); steel-plant construction (INR 10 lakh cr sector capex over 5–6 yrs).
- Coal gasification (govt INR 37,500 cr) — early-stage tracking.
- International: ~INR 300–350 cr Middle East O&M (1,500 headcount), Nigeria captive O&M (~INR 100 cr), West Africa expansion (Senegal, Liberia).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Blended FY26 EBITDA 12.3% (incl other income). O&M 15–16%; construction/erection/civil <8–10%; MDO 15–16% now → 20% peak.
- Domestic input inflation (steel, cement, diesel) largely passed through via PVC/escalation clauses; international is pure O&M manpower so insulated. West-Asia war: minimal impact (intl only 1.2–1.5% of OB, ~4–5% revenue export mix).
- Margin uplift thesis = rising O&M + MDO + EPC mix.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Low leverage (D/E 0.32x); strong OCF turnaround (INR 430 cr). MDO/Tasra capex funded without incremental debt at parent. Focus on shifting mix toward higher-margin recurring O&M to lift profitability and reduce working-capital borrowing.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, bullish, granular on numbers — CFO gave specific mine economics, margin bridges, and candidly acknowledged the order-inflow miss and the MDO guidance cut (conservative framing). Transparent on water-division drag. Tone credible; repeatedly emphasized power-sector visibility to FY30 and O&M-led margin improvement.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- Order-inflow guidance reliability (missed FY26 by ~28%; BESS cancellation). Verify FY27 INR 12,000 cr inflow tracking.
- MDO ramp risk — guidance already cut; CCL washery dependency, monsoon seasonality, single-month (March) revenue spike not sustainable run-rate.
- Water division receivable/certification overhang (central-govt fund release dependent).
- Labor availability (40,000+ headcount, 70–75% labor; civil labor from WB/Odisha/Jharkhand/UP) and attrition.
- BHEL packaging-philosophy change could pressure pricing/qualification on installation orders.
- Commodity inflation on fixed-price portions not covered by PVC.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The MDO FY28 guidance was quietly cut ~35% (INR ~1,850 cr → INR 1,250 cr) vs the Feb-26 call — a key negative not flagged in the opening remarks.
- March-26 MDO revenue (INR 117 cr) was an exceptional client-driven offtake spike; normalized run-rate is INR 40–50 cr/month — investors extrapolating Q4 MDO (INR 226 cr) would overstate FY27.
- "EPC" segment now replaces the discontinued Transmission/Electricals division; railway work folded into civil — segment-label change, not pure new growth.
- The thermal thesis is explicitly a renewable-integration play: management argues 150→300GW solar creates grid imbalance requiring more thermal for night/day-night operation — a contrarian-sounding but coherent grid-stability argument.
- Receivables-driven OCF jump (74 lakh → 430 cr) is the single biggest balance-sheet positive and underappreciated vs the headline order-miss narrative.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- vs Feb-26 (Q3 FY26) call: **MDO FY28 guidance cut** from INR 1,800–1,900 cr to INR 1,250 cr (conservative ramp; CCL washery not ready).
- Segment relabel: discontinued **Transmission/Electricals** division; railway portfolio moved into **Civil**; new **BOP EPC** line added.
- FY26 order inflow INR 7,210 cr vs INR 10,000 cr target (72%) — primary miss = INR 1,563 cr WB BESS cancellation (to be re-tendered FY27).
- New L1 wins surfaced: Bangalore Metro, Monorail (April).
- FY27 order inflow target raised to INR 12,000 cr (FY26 target was 10,000).
- OCF jumped from INR 74 lakh (FY25) to INR 430 cr (FY26).
- New gratuity provision INR 4.5 cr (Labor Code basic 40%→50%).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Margin drivers] Management attributes the margin decline to "an increase in royalty costs in the KRBM project following the Government Order on royalty sharing for seized quantities, higher OB removal costs at the KBP mine and increased material costs due to the ongoing middle east conflict" - the royalty change is a regulatory event, and the OB removal spend is described as "higher OB removal costs to make new seams accessible for future production and ramp-up".
- [Backlog composition] The order backlog breakup is overwhelmingly MDO (INR 39,330 Cr of INR 55,398 Cr on the chart's labelling), with the balance across Civil Infra, O&M, Industrial EPC and Industrial Construction; note the deck elsewhere sizes operationalized MDO contracts at INR 39,169 Cr, a different figure.
- [Backlog growth] Order backlog including MDO is shown as 23,027 / 57,053 / 53,994 / 55,151 / 55,398 for FY23 / FY24 / FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27 - i.e. broadly flat since the MDO step-up in FY24, with annual order inflow of 8,479 / 8,314 / 6,347 / 7,210 across FY23-FY26.
- [Group structure] The leadership team includes whole-time directors for KTMPL, KBP Mining and PM Green Pvt. Ltd, indicating mining and green-energy activity is housed in separate entities; consolidated PAT carries a material non-controlling interest (INR 47.69 Cr in FY26 against INR 21.07 Cr in FY25).
- [Governance] The board is weighted with power-sector veterans - a non-executive director with 38+ years at BHEL and an independent director with 37+ years at BHEL including over 6 years as Chairman & MD, plus an independent director with 40+ years in Indian infrastructure.
